# X-Robots-Tag

*Directive*

An HTTP response header that carries robots rules such as noindex, so they also work for PDFs, images and other non-HTML files.

**Glossary** (*X-Robots-Tag*): An HTTP header that carries the same rules as the robots meta tag, also for files that are not HTML. Like the tag, Google only sees it on URLs it is allowed to crawl.

Narrative: the topic [Robots meta tags and noindex](../topics/robots-meta-tag.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

4 claims mention it: 3 from Google's documentation, 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag).

- [`D2-C069`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Docs: Google's robots meta tag specification says robots meta tags and X-Robots-Tag headers are found only when a URL is crawled, so the rules on a URL disallowed in robots.txt are never seen and are ignored. `[D2-C069, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag]`
- [`D2-C095`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Docs: Google's Search documentation gives notranslate as a rule for a robots or googlebot meta tag or an X-Robots-Tag header, and says the rule opts a page out of all translation features in Google Search. `[D2-C095, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/translated-results]`
- [`D2-C529`](../sessions/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) Docs: Google's documented ways to keep a site's images out of search results are a robots.txt disallow rule (for example for Googlebot-Image) or a noindex X-Robots-Tag HTTP header, with the Removals tool for emergencies. `[D2-C529, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/prevent-images-on-your-page]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C530`](../sessions/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) Analysis: Hiding an image as a CSS background is a fragile way to keep it out of Google: it only stops extraction from that page, so the same image URL used in an img element elsewhere or listed in a sitemap can still be indexed; the documented robots.txt or noindex X-Robots-Tag methods are the reliable route. `[D2-C530, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-IDX-03` **SHOULD** · Documented: Send robots rules for PDFs, images and other non-HTML files in the X-Robots-Tag header (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IDX-09` **SHOULD** · Documented: Leave notranslate and noimageindex out of templates unless translation or image indexing must be prevented (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IMG-06` **SHOULD** · Documented: Keep images out of Search with robots.txt or X-Robots-Tag, not with CSS tricks (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
